[QUERENT] What is SPXI Protocol?

[ANSWER]

“SPXI protocol” isn’t a universally recognized technical standard, and its meaning depends on the context. It may be a typo or a specialized term.
One possibility is that you mean IPX/SPX, a legacy computer networking protocol used with Novell NetWare networks.
[image](https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=https://en.wikipedia.org&sz=32)
Wikipedia
+1

* IPX (Internetwork Packet Exchange): Handles addressing and routing data packets.
* SPX (Sequenced Packet Exchange): Provides reliable, ordered delivery of data between devices.
* Modern equivalent: TCP/IP largely replaced IPX/SPX in computer networks.

There is also a newer, specialized meaning: SPXI = Semantic Packet for eXchange & Indexing. Its published specification describes a framework for helping AI search systems identify entities—such as people, organizations, products, and concepts—more accurately, using structured information and provenance records.
[image](https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=https://www.spxi.dev&sz=32)
Semantic Packet for eXchange & Indexing
For example, it aims to help AI systems distinguish between two organizations with similar names or identify the correct source and creator of a concept.
You can read the published specification at [SPXI.dev ](https://www.spxi.dev/?utm_source=chatgpt.com).
Which context did you encounter SPXI in? AI search/SEO, computer networking, or somewhere else? I can explain the relevant version in more detail.
